title: Every finite original sampled lower-exit infimum has arbitrarily close true violating observations
author: @WillR
source: The infimum t is no greater than each qualifying sampled time. If every qualifying sampled time lay at or above t+ε, the complete-lattice infimum would also be at least t+ε, contradicting ε>0. This is exactly the missing sample-selection step needed before the proved right-continuous endpoint-contact limit.

title: Lemma 4.1 — one improvement step: a dense ball, a more scattered subset, or a $(3d,2)$-shallow induced 1-subdivided $K_h$
author: @Shuze Chen
source: Filtser, Le, Mählmann, Ma. Pilipczuk, Mi. Pilipczuk, Fatness and Flatness, arXiv:2607.21474, Lemma 4.1, p. 12 (PDF p. 14). Verbatim: 'Lemma 4.1. Let h, d be positive integers with d ⩾ 2, let G be a graph, and A ⊆ V(G) be a 2d-scattered set in G of size at least 4^5(h+1)^10. Then, one of the following holds: • There exists v ∈ V(G) such that |A ∩ Ball_G(v, d+6)| ⩾ |A|^{1/10}. • There exists B ⊆ A of size at least |A|^{1/10} that is 2(d+1)-scattered in G. • There exists a (3d,2)-shallow induced model of the 1-subdivision of K_h in G.' source: Filtser, Le, Mählmann, Ma. Pilipczuk, Mi. Pilipczuk, Fatness and Flatness, arXiv:2607.21474, Lemma 6.4, p. 18 (PDF p. 20). Verbatim: 'Lemma 6.4 (Fan lemma). For every r ∈ N there exists a function F : N → N with the following property. Let G be a graph, o ∈ V(G), m ∈ N, and X ⊆ V(G) be a set of at least F(m) vertices, each at distance at most r from o.
